newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Rain over the weekend has increased the chances for many leading horses in tomorrow's A$2.2 million Foster's Melbourne Cup. Trainer of Cup favourite Oscar Schindler, Kevin Prendergast, had considered scratching the horse if the ground didn't soften, while the chances of the Freedman brothers winning their fourth Cup with last year's champion Doriemus have increased with the softening of the track. Page 19.

Australia's rugby union side, the Wallabies, notched up another victory on their tour of Europe against the Combined Scottish Districts 37-19, but were criticised by the locals, who alleged the team used illegal tactics. Combined Districts coach Kevin Grene said the Australians' rolling maul, used so well, should have been deemed illegal. Page 21.

Australian Cricket Board chief executive Graham Halbish revealed over the weekend that Australia's many one-day internationals will see the team's top six players earn more than A$300,000 each from direct match payments. Page 28.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As the West Indies cricket side, here to compete for the Frank Worrell trophy and in the World Series Cup one-day matches, warmed up in practice nets in Perth yesterday, all eyes were on fast bowler Patterson Thompson, who is touted as the fastest bowler n the world. Page 29.

Miles Stewart, who won the Triathlon World Series closer at Noosa Heads yesterday, was disappointed to learn that Brazilian Alexandre Mansion would not be competing in the event, as his focus was on beating Manzan. However, Stewart still found the inspiration to win the event in one hour, 46 minutes and two seconds. Page 31.

The South East Melbourne Magic basketball team easily ended the Melbourne Tigers' hopes of winning back to back National Basketball League titles with a 107-70 win in the deciding third game of the grand final series at Melbourne Park yesterday. The
Magic successfully defended Tigers point scorer Andrew Gaze. Page 31.
THE AGE

Irish jockey Michael Kinane, here to ride Melbourne Cup favourite Oscar Schindler, has arrived in Australia early without the knowledge of the Victorian Racing Committee. Kinane cancelled his hotel booking made by the VRC and is known to be keen to avoidthe Australian racing media after being criticised for his 1994 ride of previous champion Vintage Crop. Page 2.

The Australian cricket team is in trouble in its Titan Cup match against India in Chandigrah after the Indian side scored its highest one-day total of 6/289. Sachin Tendulkar and Mohammed Azharuddin were the best of the Indians after Australia's specialit bowlers gave them too much width. Australia later lost in the last over, falling six runs short. Page 2.

The Collingwood Warriors soccer team defeated West Adelaide 2-1 at Hindmarsh Stadium last night, helped along by strong performances from Rick Cerracchio, who scored two goals, and goalkeeper Frank Juric. The win sees Collingwood so far unbeaten in the Eicsson Cup. Page 19.
HERALD SUN

The Melbourne Monarchs baseball team have been boosted by the unexpected early arrival of Damian Moss, who is tipped to be the next Australian player to play in the overseas major leagues. Melbourne manager Jon Deebie said it was possible Moss
would be included on the roster to play against the Adelaide Giants. Page 85.

The South Melbourne soccer team has suffered its second home game defeat of the season, going down to the Brisbane Strikers 2-1. The team has not yet won a match in the Ericsson Cup, placing further pressure on coach Angie Postecoglou. Page 85.

South East Melbourne Magic basketball player Mike Kelly was awarded the Most Valuable Player of the finals series after his side defeated the Melbourne Tigers by 37 points yesterday. Three years ago, the American Kelly was playing in the CBA after being gnored by the NBL. Page 84.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The New South Wales 18-footer sailing championships were held on Sydney Harbour yesterday, with defending champion Chris Nicholson, along with his crew of Daniel Phillips and Gary Boyd, steering his skiff Skilled Engineer to victory in "fresh to
frightening" conditions. Page 37.

New South Wales rugby union captain Tim Gavin has finally been given a chance to play for the Wallabies in their tour of Britain and Ireland after Mark Connors suffered serious knee damage in the match in Glasgow. However, Gavin was not the selectors' fist choice - he was only selected because Willie Ofahengaue failed a fitness test. Page 39.

Australian netball coach Jill McIntosh organised a two-day training camp for her squad of 12 which will face New Zealand on November 16, with the main focus being a game against the Australian under-21 side which lasted for 90 minutes rather than the usual 60. Page 58.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
